key_insight: Understanding a scene requires more than recognizing what is currently visible: an AI must also track what is out of view as its viewpoint changes. This paper probes whether visual foundation models contain representations that support this persistent spatial state; the provided abstract does not report findings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to assess whether visual foundation models represent a coherent spatial world beyond individual images, including hidden objects and changes caused by observer motion.
method: Probe visual foundation model representations for capabilities supporting a persistent spatial state.
Organize the investigation into four capability levels; the excerpt names spatial structure, object persistence, and predictive spatial updating.
Examine spatial state in the context of partial observations and observer motion; the fourth level and experimental details are not included in the excerpt.
impact: This evaluation perspective could help practitioners distinguish image-recognition ability from spatial understanding relevant to navigation and embodied AI. Model comparisons and practical performance gains cannot be determined from the provided excerpt.
